request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias now merges them into that person instead of refusing the transfer. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **`PersonTransferService`**: before moving the person, it looks on the other sheet for anyone matching their name or any of their aliases. The match ignores case and skips people already merged away.
  - **One match:** the person is transferred as before (claims renumbered there, figures bound by statements lost), then merged into the match. The other sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its rollup lines.
  - **No match:** behaves exactly as before, including the existing name, alias and contact checks.
- **`PersonMergeService`**: I moved the body of `merge` into a package-private `absorb(...)` so the transfer can reuse it. Its steward check is skipped there, because the transfer already checked that the user is a steward on the source sheet.
- **New migration `V76__person_alias_not_unique.sql`**: the store had a unique index on sheet + lower-cased alias. The test expects Ada to end up with both `Addie` and `addie` as aliases, which that index made impossible, so I replaced it with a non-unique index of the same name. Adding an alias through the screen is still refused when it's already in use, because the service checks for that itself.

**Choices the request didn't specify** — change these if you want different behaviour:
- If the arriving person's names match **more than one** person on the other sheet, the transfer is refused, since it's unclear who to merge into.
- If the match is **retired**, the transfer is refused, in line with the existing rule that nobody merges into a retired person.
- When a merge happens, the arriving person's contact is **not** checked against the other sheet, because a merge drops it anyway.

The javadocs on both services and on `TransferRefusedException` are updated to match.
